title: Trade Planning and Review
summary: Plan, record and review each trade, judging process and result apart. Education only, not advice.

modules.title: Writing the Thesis and the Trade Plan
modules.subject: Trade planning
modules.learned: Write a thesis with its invalidation and complete a one-page plan before an order is sent.

check.q: A trader writes that a chart looks strong and feels right. Why is this not a usable thesis?
options: It names no evidence and no invalidation, so the trade cannot be tested
It is too short, so it should be longer
It is correct, because confidence is the key input
It should be written after the result instead
check.explanation: A usable thesis names the evidence and the specific event that would prove it wrong, so the result can be judged.

modules.title: Targets, R-Multiples and Partial Exits
modules.subject: Targets and results
modules.learned: Set a target by a written rule, express results in R, and explain the trade-off of a partial exit.

check.q: A buy has an entry of 40.00, a stop at 39.00 and a target at 42.00. What is the reward-to-risk ratio?
check.explanation: The target is 2.00 from entry and the stop is 1.00 away, so the target distance divided by the stop distance is 2.0.

modules.title: The Trade Journal
modules.subject: Journaling
modules.learned: List the core, decision and context fields of a trade journal, and keep feelings separate from facts.

check.q: A trader keeps a journal but fills in the stop only after the trade closes, from memory. What is the main risk?
options: Memory always records trades more accurately
The broker will refuse the record
The record can drift to match the outcome, so the review cannot judge the plan
It costs more time than a paper journal
check.explanation: Facts recorded after the outcome tend to fit the result. Recording the plan before the trade keeps the review honest.

modules.title: Process Versus Outcome in Review
modules.subject: Process review
modules.learned: Separate the quality of a decision from its result, classify trades, and avoid hindsight bias.

check.q: A trader followed her plan exactly and lost 1R. How should the review classify the trade?
options: A poor process, because the trade lost money
A lucky trade, because a loss cannot be lucky
A reason to double the size next time
A good process with a normal loss, which does not on its own justify changing the plan
check.explanation: The review judges the decision. A planned loss within normal variation does not, on its own, justify changing a sound plan.

modules.title: Scoreboard: Adherence, Expectancy and Cost
modules.subject: Performance metrics
modules.learned: Calculate plan adherence and expectancy in R, read the spread of results, and recognise a sample that is too small.

check.q: A trader's plan adherence falls from 90 percent to 70 percent over a month, while results look good. What does this signal?
options: A process problem to review, even though results look good
A certain loss in the next month
That the market has become unsuitable for trading
That the journal should be stopped
check.explanation: A falling adherence rate is a process signal. A process that is often broken cannot be relied on to keep producing results.

modules.title: Weekly and Monthly Review with a Change Log
modules.subject: Review and change control
modules.learned: Run a fixed weekly and monthly review, log every plan change with its evidence, and test changes on new trades.

check.q: After a bad week, a trader wants to widen her stop at once. What is the right response under a change log?
options: Widen the stop at once, because the bad week shows the plan is wrong
Log the concern, test the wider stop on new trades, and adopt it only if the sample supports it
Stop trading until she feels better about the plan
Delete the bad week from the journal
check.explanation: A change after a bad week is suspect. A tested change, with the old version kept in the record, answers the concern without guessing.

questions.q: Why must a trade's invalidation be written before entry?
options: So a bad trade can be told apart from one that is merely slow
Because brokers require it on every order
So the stop can be moved after entry
Because invalidation replaces the time horizon

questions.q: Which is the best example of a usable thesis?
options: The chart looks strong and I feel confident
Price has held above a support area for three weeks, so buyers are defending it, and a close below the area proves it wrong
Everyone online is buying, so it should rise
The market will go up because it has gone down

questions.q: A trader's order is ready, but the target field is empty. What should happen next?
options: Send the order and set the target later
Send the order and leave the target blank
Fill the target from the plan's rule, check the ratio, then send the order
Skip the trade because the target cannot be known

questions.q: Which check should be run before an order is sent?
options: The broker's logo matches the brand
The idea has many followers online
The chart looks confident to the trader
The stop is on the losing side of entry and the cash risk fits the budget

questions.q: A trader fills in the thesis after the trade has closed. What is the main problem?
options: The thesis now fits the result, so the decision cannot be judged fairly
Nothing, because the thesis is only a formality
It is better, because the result is already known
Brokers require plans to be written after the trade

questions.q: A buy has an entry of 40.00, a stop at 39.00 and a target at 42.00. What is the reward-to-risk ratio?
What is one R?
options: The total cash in the account
The commission paid on the trade
The cash risk on the trade, used as the unit for its result
The distance from entry to target

questions.q: A trade risks 100 USD and makes 250 USD. What is its result in R?
options: Plus 250R
Plus 1.5R
Minus 2.5R
Plus 2.5R

questions.q: What is the main trade-off of a partial exit?
options: It reduces the swing in results but also limits the size of a large win
It removes all risk from the trade
It guarantees the second target will be reached
It doubles the expected profit

questions.q: Why should a target be set before entry?
options: Because the target predicts the exact top of the move
So the exit decision is made in advance, not under pressure
Because brokers require a target on every order
So the target can be moved after each good candle

questions.q: What are the three groups of fields in a trade journal?
options: Cash, tax and currency
Entry, exit and commission only
Core facts, decision fields and context fields
Feelings, rumours and forecasts

questions.q: Why should feelings be recorded in their own place?
options: Because feelings are the most important field
Because brokers ban emotional notes
So the feeling can be used to choose the next entry
So they do not alter the facts of the trade and the numbers stay trustworthy

questions.q: A trader deletes losing trades from the journal to make it look better. What is the main problem?
options: The record hides the process, so the review cannot find what went wrong
A cleaner record is always more useful
Deleting losers improves the average result
Losing trades do not need to be recorded

questions.q: What does a decision field show that a result field does not?
options: The exact profit in cash
Whether the plan was followed, which can be judged apart from the outcome
The broker's commission
The market's direction for the next week

questions.q: Which entry belongs in the context fields?
options: The final result in R
The exit price of the trade
The timeframe, and any scheduled release on the day of the trade
The trader's emotions in one line

questions.q: Which group is the most dangerous for a trader's habits?
options: A good process with a poor result
A poor process with a poor result
A good process with a good result
A poor process with a good result, because it reinforces a habit that later loses money

questions.q: A trader wins a trade that broke her volume rule. What should the review record?
options: A lucky result, flagged, with the broken rule noted
A good trade to repeat
Proof that the volume rule is too strict
Nothing, because a win needs no review

questions.q: Which is the first question in a review?
options: What was the final cash result?
Was the plan followed at entry and during the trade?
How did the trader feel?
What will the market do next week?

questions.q: Why judge an entry only with the information available at entry?
options: Because later information is never relevant
Because the broker only records entry data
To avoid hindsight bias, which makes a decision look better or worse than it was
To make every review shorter

questions.q: In a trade review, what is process?
options: The final cash result of the trade
The broker's execution speed alone
The number of trades taken in a month
The quality of the decisions taken, judged against the written plan

questions.q: A trader took 30 trades in a month, and 22 followed the plan. What is her plan adherence?
options: About 73 percent
22 percent
30 percent
8 percent

questions.q: A trade costs 0.1R and the expectancy before costs is 0.2R. What is the expectancy after costs?
options: 0.3R per trade
0.1R per trade
0.2R per trade
Minus 0.1R per trade

questions.q: Why read the spread of results, not only the average?
options: The spread shows the broker's fees
An average is always misleading, so the spread replaces it
A few large losses can produce a poor result even when most trades are small winners
The spread is required by regulators

questions.q: What is the main sign of a sample that is too small to read?
options: A positive average R for the month
More than one trade in a day
A plan adherence above 70 percent
A conclusion drawn from only a handful of trades, which may reflect chance

questions.q: A scoreboard shows a positive average R, and the trader wants to double the size. What should be checked first?
options: Adherence and the split of results between planned and unplanned trades
The broker's advertised returns
The number of followers on social media
The weather on the day of the trade

questions.q: What should a change log entry always contain?
options: Only the new rule and the date
The date, the version number, the reason, the evidence and the test plan
Only the trader's name and the broker
Only the result of the last trade

questions.q: Why is a change made after a bad week suspect?
options: Because changes are never allowed in trading
Because bad weeks always reverse
Recent losses pull judgement towards recency bias, so the change may miss the real problem
Because the journal cannot be updated during a bad week

questions.q: How should a proposed change to a plan be tested?
options: On the trades that suggested the change
By applying it at once to all open positions
By asking friends whether the rule sounds good
On new trades, against the current version, with the old rule kept in the record

questions.q: What does a monthly review look at, compared with a weekly review?
options: Trends across the period, and whether the sample is large enough to read
Each trade's entry price, one at a time
Only the broker's fees
Only the trader's emotions in the journal

questions.q: Which practice keeps a plan change auditable?
options: Overwriting the plan so the latest version is the only one
Keeping each version with a number and linking each trade to the version it used
Changing several rules at once to save time
Deleting old versions after each month
